title: quest overview reports milestone counts that silently exclude archived milestones, the same unlabelled narrowing as QCLI-339
description:
Ruled by opum-agent 2026-09-18 as the second half of the QCLI-339 ruling: overview must not report a count whose object is narrower than the object a reader takes it for.

ProjectManager.overview counts milestones as open or closed with item.archived !== true on both filters, so an archived milestone counts as NEITHER. That exclusion is deliberate per QCLI-140 (retire without destroying) and is stated in a code comment, but nothing in the OUTPUT says so. It is the identical defect to QCLI-339, in the same function, two lines below the task counts that were just fixed.

Filed on the orchestrator ruling rather than on a live instance. This repository has 1 open, 0 closed, 0 archived milestones, so there is no measured wrong number here today. The argument for doing it now rather than deferring: an empty population is the argument FOR a shape fix, not against it. The cost will never be lower, and the alternative is that the first workspace to archive a milestone gets a silently wrong count with nobody watching.

Scope note: this does NOT reopen QCLI-140. Archived milestones remain retired and must not be counted as open or closed work. The fix is to make the exclusion visible and countable, not to fold archived milestones back into open/closed.

acceptanceCriteria.text: quest overview reports how many milestones are archived, so the excluded population is visible in the output rather than only in a code comment
An archived milestone is still counted as neither open nor closed, so QCLI-140 is preserved rather than reopened; asserted by a test that archives a milestone and checks open and closed both stay put
The decisions counts are audited for the same narrowing and either fixed or recorded as not affected, with the reason stated
Any JSON addition sits inside data, leaving contractVersion at index 1 and principal as the last top-level key
A mutation of the implementation reddens a predicted subset of the new tests, with the prediction derived from reading the test file before running it

implementationNotes: CORRECTING MY OWN BASIS FOR FILING THIS. I told the orchestrator there was no live instance in this repository (1 open, 0 closed, 0 archived milestones), and filed on their ruling rather than on a measurement. That was wrong in a way I found while writing the tests: the existing planning suite ALREADY constructs an archived milestone. After its cleanup step, M-1 is archived and the pre-existing assertion read open 0 / closed 0 with nothing indicating a milestone existed at all. So a measured case was sitting in the test file the whole time, one function away from the code I had just changed. I looked at the repositorys .quest/planning.json and concluded there was no instance; the object I should also have looked at was the test fixture. Same class as the QCLI-339 evidence error found the same hour: I checked one population and reported a conclusion about a wider one.

DECISIONS AUDITED, NOT ASSUMED (criterion 3). A Decision record has no archived field at all; its statuses are proposed, accepted and superseded, and overview counts every decision grouped by status with no filter. So superseded is a REPORTED status rather than a hidden exclusion and the decisions count already covers every record. Not affected, and now pinned by a test so a future archived field on decisions cannot repeat this silently.

MUTATION PROOF, both red subsets predicted from reading the test file before running. M1, archived forced to a constant 0: predicted tests 1 and 2 red (both assert the archived count) with tests 3 and 4 green; measured exactly that, 2 fail 2 pass. M2 is the one that matters, because it is the WRONG fix wearing the right shape -- drop the archived guard from the closed filter so an archived milestone counts as closed, which makes the narrowing go away by reopening QCLI-140: predicted ONLY test 2 red, since test 1 archives an OPEN milestone and is blind to that change; measured exactly that, 1 fail 3 pass. That is the evidence the suite separates making the exclusion visible from abolishing the exclusion, which are the two things this task had to keep apart.

SUPPORTING CONTRAST found while fixing a test: milestone list narrows the SAME way and says so, both in its help text (excluding archived ones by default) and by offering --include-archived to widen it. overview had neither the label nor the widening flag. That is what made this a defect rather than a style preference, and it is asserted in the test rather than left as prose.
finalSummary:
overview milestone counts now report archived alongside open and closed, so the excluded population is visible in the output instead of only in a code comment. QCLI-140 is preserved, not reopened: a retired milestone is still counted as neither open nor closed work.

WHAT CHANGED. ProjectManager.overview filtered both the open and closed counts with archived !== true, so an archived milestone counted as neither and open plus closed silently summed to less than the milestones on record. Added an archived count beside them, and a doc comment on ProjectOverview saying why the exclusion exists and why it is now reported. Decisions were AUDITED rather than assumed and are not affected: a Decision record has no archived field, and superseded is one of its three reported statuses rather than a hidden exclusion.

TWO THINGS THIS HAD TO KEEP APART, and the mutation proof is what shows it does. Making the exclusion VISIBLE is the fix; ABOLISHING the exclusion by folding archived into closed would also make the narrowing disappear and would reopen QCLI-140. M2 mutates exactly that way -- drop the archived guard from the closed filter -- and reddens ONLY the QCLI-140 preservation test, predicted before running because test 1 archives an open milestone and is blind to it. Measured 1 fail 3 pass. M1, archived forced to a constant 0, was predicted to redden tests 1 and 2 and did, 2 fail 2 pass. Both predictions were derived from reading the test file and both matched exactly.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN FILING BASIS. I told the orchestrator there was no live instance here (1 open, 0 closed, 0 archived milestones) and filed on their ruling alone. A measured case was already in the test fixture: after the planning suite cleanup step, M-1 is archived, and the pre-existing assertion read open 0 / closed 0 with nothing indicating a milestone existed. I checked .quest/planning.json and reported a conclusion about a wider population than I had looked at.

SUPPORTING CONTRAST. milestone list narrows the same way and SAYS SO, in its help (excluding archived ones by default) and by offering --include-archived. overview had neither, which is what makes this a defect rather than a preference. Asserted in the test rather than left as prose.

HOW IT WAS VERIFIED. bun run check exits 0, 581 pass 0 fail. Four new end-to-end tests spawn the real CLI against a real workspace; three pre-existing shape assertions (planning overview, the retired-milestone case, and the browser payload) correctly failed on the addition and were updated, which is itself evidence the shape is asserted somewhere rather than unpinned. Envelope assertions confirm contractVersion at index 1 and principal last, as two separate assertions because presence and position fail on different edits.
